source_artifacts.claim: Defines the Isp-held dual gate, two hero exits, bubble projectile started by HOLD, and route hint.
A bubble hit gives Isp FLOAT and Pac STICKY; a top bounce is handled separately.
The HOLD pad starts the bubble attack; its configured cooldown and windup govern repeated bubbles.
Pac bounces if descending onto the bubble from above; other bubble contacts apply their hero-specific effect.
STICKY suppresses movement and jump input temporarily; FLOAT alters the normal jump path.
An occupied Isp-held pad opens every barrier effect attached to it.
Isp and Pac have separate WASD and arrow-key movement/jump bindings.

At position 19, Gem's Bubble Break introduced Isp bubble FLOAT and Pac bubble-top bounce, in separate route roles.

evidence.claim: Position 2 explicitly tells Isp to hold a door for Pac and supplies the corresponding pad/barrier route.

prior_knowledge.concept: Gem bubbles can FLOAT Isp and Pac can bounce from their gold tops; this room requires first using Pac's bounce role, then allowing Isp to receive FLOAT.

evidence.claim: Position 19 introduces Pac bubble-top bounce and Isp FLOAT; the current room recombines the two roles.

prior_knowledge.concept: One hero's hold can release two separate gates, while a bubble serves first as Pac's repeated bounce surface and later as Isp's lift.

evidence.claim: HOLD opens both Pac barriers and starts the bubble stream in this combined sequence.

mechanics.fact: Isp stands on HOLD; this one pad opens both barriers that block Pac. It also starts Gem's repeated bubble attack. Isp must remain while Pac passes both barriers, then can leave after Pac is above the bubble path.

evidence.claim: Isp-only HOLD opens both Pac gates and starts the bubble attack.
An occupied hold pad applies both door effects.

mechanics.fact: Pac catches bubbles from above to bounce repeatedly over the two tall barriers and reach the lower exit/shelf. A side or direct hit instead gives Pac STICKY; after Pac clears the projectile path, a later bubble can hit Isp and give FLOAT for 1.4 seconds so Isp can reach the upper ledge and exit.

evidence.claim: The route hint describes Pac catching bubbles to advance, then letting one hit Isp for FLOAT to the upper ledge.
The bubble stream starts on HOLD and repeats rapidly.
Isp's FLOAT duration is 1.4 seconds.
Pac bounces from above, while other contact applies the appropriate hero effect.

mechanics.fact: There are no hazards or collectibles; the lower floor is continuous, while the two matching exits are separate and both required.

evidence.claim: The room has a continuous lower floor, no hazards or collectibles, upper ledge, and two hero exits.

legal_routes.name: Pac bounces through; then Isp takes a later bubble to the upper exit

steps.goal: Open both Pac gates and start the bubble stream.
steps.action: Move to and hold the Isp-only HOLD pad; stay there until Pac clears the barriers and reaches the last shelf.
steps.expected_feedback: Both Pac gates open, and Gem sends recurring bubbles along the room's low route.
steps.observed_feedback: The scripted input first moves Isp onto the pad and leaves Isp there while Pac passes the two gates and reaches the shelf/exit.

evidence.claim: The pad effect and gates are defined.
Isp moves to the hold position before Pac proceeds.

steps.goal: Use bubbles as repeated bounces to cross the gates and reach Pac's exit/shelf.
steps.action: Move right and jump onto the top of each bubble as it passes, continuing across entry and far barriers to the shelf near Pac's lower exit.
steps.expected_feedback: A top hit gives Pac a bounce rather than the side-hit STICKY effect; the repeated stream supplies further attempts.
steps.observed_feedback: In the scripted route Pac moves to the far gate, reaches the shelf and enters Pac's exit while Isp remains at HOLD; the route log does not record individual bubble collisions.

evidence.claim: Pac's descending top contact with a bubble produces a bounce.
Pac reaches the lower exit before Isp begins the upper crossing.

steps.goal: Let a later bubble hit Isp and use FLOAT to reach the upper route.
steps.action: After Pac is above/clear of the bubble path, leave HOLD and allow a later bubble to hit Isp; steer right during FLOAT to the upper ledge and Isp exit.
steps.expected_feedback: A bubble hit gives Isp FLOAT; the 1.4-second lift is enough to reach the elevated platform if Isp steers across.
steps.observed_feedback: After Pac reaches the shelf/exit, the scripted route has Isp rise from the HOLD area, move along the upper ledge, and reach Isp's exit.

evidence.claim: The hint supplies the sequence of letting a bubble hit Isp and steering right during FLOAT.
Isp is above the HOLD area after Pac has reached the shelf.
Final phase reaches both exits with zero deaths.
Room definition and route hint support the bubble/hold sequence.

isp: Move onto HOLD and keep both Pac gates open while Pac advances. When Pac is above the bubble path, allow a later bubble to hit Isp for FLOAT, then steer to the upper exit.
pac: Use repeated bubble-top bounces to cross the two gates and reach Pac's lower exit/shelf, then clear the bubble path so Isp can use a later bubble to float to the upper exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp leaves HOLD before Pac has passed the far gate.
common_mistakes.consequence: Both gates close and Pac is blocked from finishing the required lower route.
common_mistakes.recovery: Isp can return to HOLD so the gates reopen; the continuous floor and repeated bubble stream support a local retry. The provided successful run did not test this failure.

evidence.claim: The held pad opens both gates and its effect depends on occupancy.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac contacts a bubble from the side/below instead of landing on its top, or keeps catching every bubble after reaching the shelf.
common_mistakes.consequence: A side hit temporarily makes Pac STICKY; catching every later bubble prevents Isp from receiving the FLOAT needed for the upper route.
common_mistakes.recovery: STICKY wears off after 0.6 seconds and bubbles repeat; Pac can reposition and stop intercepting so a subsequent bubble reaches Isp. No human mistake or recovery was observed.

evidence.claim: STICKY lasts 0.6 seconds.
Only Pac's descending top contact bounces; another contact applies a temporary effect.
The bubbles repeat after a short cooldown.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp allows a bubble to hit before Pac is above the beam/shelf area.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp may float without a useful landing/steering path and need another bubble to make the upper route.
common_mistakes.recovery: Return to HOLD/lower floor and wait for the next repeated bubble; the room has no lethal hazard and the path remains available. This plausible retry is source-derived; no failure was observed.

evidence.claim: The hint conditions Isp's FLOAT attempt on Pac first being above the beam.
Continuous floor and upper platform support safe regrouping.

reasoning.rationale: The route requires a non-obvious ordered use of the same repeated bubble stream: Pac catches bubble tops to cross two gates, then stops intercepting once above the beam so Isp can receive a later bubble and FLOAT to the upper exit. Isp must hold both gates until Pac clears them. Familiar individual mechanics still combine into several dependent decisions.

evidence.claim: Hint and room definition establish the sequence and hold dependency.
Bubble contact has different outcomes based on hero/contact angle.

cooperation.rationale: Isp holds the two gates while Pac advances and then Pac clears the path so Isp can use a later bubble. These are distinct necessary roles with a handoff/sequenced dependency, but the route does not require repeated mutual pad operation or simultaneous movement.

evidence.claim: Isp's one pad opens both Pac gates.
Pac's route precedes Isp's later FLOAT route.

execution.rationale: Pac makes repeated controlled jumps from bubble tops across two tall gates and onto the shelf, while Isp must hold the pad and later receive/steer a FLOAT onto the high ledge. The ordinary-input route demonstrates one clear, not novice reliability or precision rates.

evidence.claim: The gates, shelf and upper exit require distinct controlled routes.
A normal-input route completes both exits.

timing.rationale: Pac needs a descending top contact on moving bubbles, and Isp later needs a 1.4-second FLOAT window to reach the upper ledge. Bubbles repeat every 0.9 seconds after the 0.75-second windup and 0.15-second cooldown, so the window is active but repeatable rather than narrow or one-shot.

evidence.claim: The bubble windup/cooldown makes recurring timing opportunities.
FLOAT lasts 1.4 seconds.
Pac must contact a bubble from above while descending to bounce.

hazards.rationale: The room defines no hazards and has a continuous floor. Bubble effects are temporary routing/interference; a Pac side-hit can briefly impede control but is not lethal or a physical danger on this route.

evidence.claim: Continuous floor and no hazards are defined.
Bubble effects are temporary FLOAT or STICKY, not a hazard in themselves.

novelty.rationale: Bubble FLOAT and Pac top-bounce were taught at position 19; a holder keeping a route open was taught in position 2. The new element is combining both roles in a sequence where Pac must first consume bubbles as bounce opportunities and later let one through for Isp, rather than learning a new object or control model.

evidence.claim: Earlier room teaches bubble effects and route split.
Earlier tutorial teaches hold-for-other-hero door role.
Current room combines held dual gates with a recurring dual-use bubble stream.

recovery_cost.rationale: There are no lethal hazards; a missed bounce, early gate release, or mistimed FLOAT can be retried from the continuous floor and recurring bubble stream. A Pac STICKY effect lasts 0.6 seconds. The successful script has no failure, so local recovery cost is inferred from repeatable mechanics rather than observed human recovery.

evidence.claim: Continuous floor and hold-triggered repeatable gate/bubble mechanism support retry.
STICKY lasts 0.6 seconds.

solution_clarity.rationale: The dialogue and subtitle cue a holder, catching bubbles, and later passage; the on-canvas legend names Pac's top-bounce and Isp's FLOAT roles. But the cue does not say Pac should stop intercepting so a later bubble can lift Isp, and the two gates' shared control becomes clear only when testing the pad or reading the hint. This leaves one important sequence inference.

evidence.claim: Canvas shows the bubble effect legend, HOLD label, gates and matching exits.
Subtitle cues catching now and letting a bubble through later; hint explains the exact route sequence.

control_friction.rationale: The runtime maps separate movement and jump keys to each hero; no conflicting assignments are present, and the supplied ordinary-input route completes both exits. This does not measure the ergonomics of a particular shared keyboard.

evidence.claim: The heroes use distinct input sets.
An ordinary-input scripted clear is recorded.

confidence_reason: Source establishes the holder's two gate effects, bubble contact differences, repeat interval, platform routes and both exits; one fresh ordinary-input route completes without deaths. No human attempt or failed recovery is available, and the route log does not record individual bubble collisions or pad transitions.

confirmed: The room does use Isp as a holder while Pac advances, and it combines bubble use with separate hero exits. The one holder really does control both Pac gates.
missed_mechanics: Pac must bounce from the top of recurring bubbles across the barriers, not merely approach or be hit by them; a side hit makes Pac briefly STICKY.
After Pac reaches the shelf/clears the bubble path, a later bubble must hit Isp to grant FLOAT for the upper route.
Isp remains at HOLD until Pac clears the gates, then takes the upper route; the level has no hazards or collectibles.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass left open whether a handoff was needed and whether bubbles only opened or affected the gates. Source shows the two gates are both controlled by Isp's single HOLD pad; bubbles are separately used for Pac's bounce and then Isp's FLOAT.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rises from 2 to 3 because the same repeated projectile must be intercepted by Pac first and intentionally allowed through later for Isp; this sequencing is a non-obvious dependency beyond identifying the holder.
Cooperation stays at 2: source confirms a distinct holder/runner role and a later bubble handoff, but no repeated mutual dependency or simultaneous pad operation is required.

Execution rises from 2 to 3 because Pac needs repeated controlled bubble-top bounces across two gates and onto the shelf, then Isp must steer during FLOAT to the upper ledge; scripted feasibility is not novice precision evidence.
Timing changes from null to 2 because top-bounce contact and the 1.4-second Isp FLOAT are active movement windows, but the bubble stream repeats rapidly after each short windup/cooldown.
Hazards changes from null to 0 because source confirms continuous floor and an empty hazard list; temporary bubble effects do not create physical danger.
Novelty stays at 2: earlier lessons cover both ingredient mechanics, while this room's new challenge is their ordered dual-use combination.
Recovery changes from null to 1 because a missed bounce or early release can be retried on safe ground with more bubbles; source supports retry but the script contains no failed attempt.

Clarity stays at 2: the subtitle, dialogue and visible effect legend cue the ingredients, but leave the important 'Pac first, then let a bubble through to Isp' sequence to be inferred or learned from the hint.
unresolved: Whether novice pairs connect 'individually addressed' with alternating bubble use, and whether Pac can reliably bounce through both gates without side contact, is not measured.
The successful script records the route and both exits, but not the individual bubble contacts, player understanding, or the real recovery experience after a missed timing opportunity.

single_operator_note: A single operator would alternate between keeping Isp on HOLD and timing Pac's jumps, then deliberately switch back to Isp for the FLOAT route; coordinating bubble interception and gate holding simultaneously adds control switching outside the two-human baseline ratings.
